title: Anti-Aging Drug Rapamycin Extends Life as Much as Dieting, New Study Shows
abstract: A 167-study analysis reveals that rapamycin prolongs lifespan as effectively as dietary restriction: reducing food intake without entering a state of malnourishment. Rapamycin extends the lifespan of lab animals and is currently being explored for its potential00258-1/fulltext) human anti-aging effects. Crucially, the meta-analysis revealed that rapamycin significantly extended lifespan, mirroring the effects of DR, suggesting rapamycin could be a viable alternative to DR for humans. While metformin has shown some anti-aging effects in simpler organisms like worms and has clear benefits for individuals with type 2 diabetes, these findings suggest that its direct impact on lifespan in healthy vertebrates may be limited. The researchers noticed that the effects of DR, rapamycin, and metformin varied considerably from one study to another. This meta-analysis provides compelling evidence that rapamycin, but not metformin, closely mirrors the lifespan-extending effects of DR. A. Rapamycin, Not Metformin, Mirrors Dietary Restriction-Driven Lifespan Extension in Vertebrates: A Meta-Analysis.
